resources.string: Shows while a call is being recorded
Stops the phone from switching the recorder off while it\'s idle
Recording laws differ by country. You are responsible for telling the other person and getting their consent where it\'s required.
Please read this before you record a call.
You choose what\'s recorded: start a recording from One Dialer\'s call screen, or turn on auto-record in One Dialer\'s settings.
Follow the law where you live
Call recording laws differ by country and region. Some places allow it when one person on the call agrees, others need everyone on the call to agree, and some don\'t allow it at all.
The other person isn\'t told that you\'re recording. You\'re responsible for telling them, getting their consent where the law requires it, and using recordings lawfully.
They\'re never uploaded. They leave this phone only if you share them.
Recording both sides needs Android 12 or later.
Records you and the other person at full volume, on the earpiece, speaker, Bluetooth or headphones. Set up once with Wireless debugging; no computer or root needed.
Settings › About phone: tap Build number 7 times
Turn on Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code, then type the code into One Recorder\'s notification
Not running. Needs Wi-Fi and Wireless debugging to start
Turns on the first time the recording service starts
In Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code. Keep that open and type the 6-digit code here.
Paired. Calls are now recorded on both sides.
Paired, but the recording service didn\'t start. Open One Recorder and tap Continue.
That didn\'t work. Keep the pairing dialog open and send the code again.
Start and stop recordings from One Dialer\'s call screen, and find them in One Dialer › Calls ⋮ › Recordings.
Both sides · tap to return to the call
After the recording service starts, Developer options, USB and Wireless debugging go off, so banking apps open. Recording keeps working
This phone refused it. On ColorOS, turn on Developer options › Disable system optimization, then tap here
Developer options and USB debugging go off after the recording service starts, so most banking apps open. This phone needs Wireless debugging to stay on
Developer options go off after the recording service starts, so many banking apps open. This phone needs USB debugging to stay on
Developer options go off after the recording service starts, so some banking apps open. This phone needs USB and Wireless debugging to stay on
This phone stops the recording service when debugging goes off, so they stay on
After a reboot away from Wi-Fi, tries for up to 2 minutes through a local hotspot. Needs Location on. May not work on every phone
Starting the recording service without Wi-Fi…
Turn on One Recorder in Accessibility and it reads the pairing code itself, then switches itself off. Android 13+: if it\'s greyed out, open App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings first
Reads the 6-digit code in Wireless debugging\'s pairing dialog so you don\'t have to type it. Reads only Settings, never taps anything, and turns itself off once paired or after 5 minutes.
Didn\'t start: connect to Wi-Fi, then tap here
Didn\'t start: Wireless debugging is off. Turn it on in Developer options (tap Build number 7 times if they\'re hidden), then come back and tap Fix
Didn\'t start: Wireless debugging didn\'t accept One Recorder. Tap here to try again, or Pair again below
If the recording service won\'t start any more. Your recordings and settings stay
Keeps USB debugging on, so the recording service keeps running when Wi-Fi goes. Some banking apps won\'t open while it\'s on
Needs Start after a reboot, so One Recorder can keep USB debugging on
Wi-Fi is back, but the recording service couldn\'t start by itself. Tap to start it again
